_about: The live headquarters' command lines, read by start_live_hq.ps1 and by scripts/start.py (scripts/live_graphics.py): one list, never copied. {streamer_port} is wilbur.config.json's streamer_port; {res_x}/{res_y} the stream's size. An argument is written exactly as it goes on the command line (its own quotes included).

_why.-PixelStreamingWebRTCNegotiateCodecs: Offer every codec (H.264, VP8, VP9, AV1) and let the browser pick one it can decode. Forced to H.264, a browser built without it got no video: Unreal logged 'Missing codec from recv codec capabilities', the page gave up after 13 s and retried every 15 s.
_why.-RCWebControlEnable: Remote Control's HTTP API (localhost only, 127.0.0.1:30010): the backend moves the scene's people from studio state.
_why.-PixelStreamingWebRTC*Bitrate, -PixelStr: The encoder's own quality. Everything runs on one machine over the loopback, so the picture is encoded at the highest quality the codec has. At the defaults (a start bitrate of 1 Mbit and a 20 Mbit ceiling) WebRTC settles low and the stream softens every edge - the Owner reads that as a lack of clarity.
_why.-ExecCmds: A development binary prints engine warnings over the picture; the stream must not show them. The game otherwise starts at scalability level 3 (High): the quality groups are asked for Epic here, where they apply to the streamed game only, and the tonemapper sharpens a little to hold detail through the stream's compression.
_why.res: The page frames the scene at 1600:840; the stream keeps that shape so clicks line up.
